traps.label: Home-page swiper slider of six Facebook-event banner images (no caption text)
traps.why: The home page is a flyer carousel of wp-block-image slides with empty alt text linking to /tickets or /events; it carries no dates or times, so anything read from here is a duplicate of an /events/ entry or an OCR guess. Not in the parser’s urls but reached at depth 1.
traps.note: Run 20261017-054812 read four OCR-only records off this page (NIGHTSHIFT Oct 17, Whos the QUEEN Oct 16, Ritual's 18TH ANNUAL Vampire Ball Oct 23, PUP NIGHT Oct 21). Two folded into their /events/ twins; NIGHTSHIFT and the Vampire Ball stood as duplicates because the /events/ twins carried a different bar ("hereticatlanta", "Ritual’s"). The failure is a second record for a night, not the read itself.

traps.label: TICKETS button under ten /events/ blocks, all href="/tickets"
traps.why: The button looks like a per-event ticket link but every one of the ten points at the same site-wide tickets page (https://hereticatlanta.com/tickets/). It is not an event and it does not identify which event it belongs to; a scraper that follows it finds a page, not a ticket for that night.

evidence.quote: TICKETS

traps.note: The events above carry that page as ticketUrl because it is what the site publishes; the trap is about not treating the button as a distinct event or as proof of a per-event link.

openQuestions.q: Should the Oct 29 "Haunted Hoedown" block count as a separate published event (single) rather than an overridden occurrence of the Thursday Country series? This file folds it in (same weekday, hours, "No Cover / Free Lessons" lines); counting it separately would make publishedEventCount 10.
